name: Narcissus
overview: Narcissus is a male individual mentioned briefly in the New Testament. He is noted for being part of the household to which the Apostle Paul sends greetings, indicating a connection to the early Christian community. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional details about his background or tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Narcissus appears once in Scripture without an accompanying meaning or divine origin. It is a proper name mentioned plainly in Romans 16:11 without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Narcissus beyond the mention of his household in Romans 16:11. No other relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Narcissus is significant primarily because Paul includes greetings to his household in his letter to the Romans, suggesting that his household was part of the early Christian fellowship. This brief mention reflects the interconnectedness of believers and the importance of Christian households in the spread of the Gospel. Though not prominent, Narcissus’s inclusion highlights the personal nature of Paul’s ministry and the communal aspect of the early church.
